title: From Spoon to Silverware: Alex Baker Turns TEG 18 Upside Down
title_candidates: From Spoon to Silverware: Alex Baker Turns TEG 18 Upside Down
Everything Reversed at Camiral: A Baker Wins, A Baker Loses
Two Holes into the Stadium: Williams Takes the Jacket, Jon Baker Takes the Spoon
106 and Still Leading: The Strangest Wire-to-Wire Win in Catalonia
theme: TEG 18 handed every man back the opposite of what he brought: the serial Spoon collector (Alex Baker, 3 prior Spoons, Spoons in 2 of the last 3) won the Trophy wire-to-wire; the reigning Spoon holder (Gregg Williams, TEG 17) won the Green Jacket by 14; and the defending Trophy champion (Jon Baker) collected the Spoon on 126 — with the two Baker brothers finishing first and last.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Barney Ronay/Tom Peck register: witty, characterful, never zany, every gag anchored to a real number
opening_hook: Open on the 2nd green of the Stadium course in R3 — the single hole where Gregg Williams took outright control of the Jacket (b09) and Jon Baker's triple bogey dropped him to the bottom of the Spoon race (b31) — then organise the report around the tournament's governing idea: everyone ended up where they usually aren't.
foreshadow: Alex Baker arrives with 1 prior Trophy win and 3 prior Wooden Spoons — including Spoons in 2 of the last 3 TEGs — and shoots 46 points on day one
Gregg Williams arrives as the reigning Wooden Spoon holder from TEG 17, and opens R1 with a quadruple bogey 9 at the 7th
Jon Baker arrives as defending Trophy champion and grabs the Jacket lead at R1 H5, holding it for 20 holes
The 2nd hole of the Stadium course, mentioned in passing as the Bakers and Williams walk off it in R3

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Alex Baker — winner, 169 pts, by 8 from John Patterson
competitions.how: Outright lead from R1 H5 and never headed across the remaining 67 holes: 46 in R1 for a 12-point cushion, 41 in R2 (still 11 clear despite the worst gross round in the Tour course's TEG history), 44 in R3 to go 12 up, and a 38 in R4 that let the margin shrink to 8 without ever threatening the result. The Stableford format did the rest — his catastrophes (11 at R2's 18th, 8 at R2's 16th, 10 at R4's 14th, 8 at R4's 17th) each cost him a maximum of the same zero, while stretches like 21 points in six holes (b04) and 17 in five (b07) banked real currency.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams — winner, +66, by 14 from David Mullin
competitions.how: Third after R1 (27 over, three back), second after R2, then took the lead outright at the 2nd hole of R3 (b09) and never gave it back: rounds of 13 and 12 over on the Stadium, against Jon Baker's collapse and Mullin's uneven fortnight, turned a level scoreline into 8 clear after R3 and 14 clear at the finish. His R4 84 gross was a personal best at the Stadium by 8 shots — and matched the course record Mullin had set 24 hours earlier.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Bottom after R1, escaped to 4th on a 39-point R2 that included 16 points in the last five holes (b16), then a triple bogey at the 2nd hole of R3 (b31) put him back on the floor and he stayed there. R3's 28 and R4's 29 — including five consecutive doubles from the 7th to the 11th (b46) and a stretch of 12 holes without a hole better than bogey until the birdie at the 13th (b48) — made it mathematically dull long before the end. The defending champion, 8 shots worse than his last visit to the Stadium.

rounds.chosen_headline: The Brothers Baker Finish First and Last
rounds.angle: Williams closes with an 84 — his Stadium personal best by 8 and a match for Mullin's day-old record — to win the Jacket by 14, while Alex Baker survives a 10 at the 14th and an 8 at the 17th to take the Trophy by 8, and Jon Baker's 29 points confirm the Spoon at 126.

players.arc: The field's most decorated Spoon collector (3 prior, two in the last three TEGs) led from the 5th hole of the tournament to the last, set the worst gross round in the Tour course's TEG history along the way, and won the Trophy by 8 without ever being headed.

Defending Trophy champion and Jacket leader for 20 holes, undone by the Stadium: a triple at R3's 2nd put him last, and 28 and 29 points over the closing rounds nailed him there at 126 — the Spoon, from the man who held the Trophy.

Arrived as reigning Wooden Spoon holder, opened with a 9 at the 7th, then made the Stadium his own — Jacket lead from R3 H2, an 84 in R4 for a course personal best by 8 shots, and a 14-shot Jacket win, his third.

Nine prior Jackets and a wretched first two days on the Tour (an 11, two 8s, 10 shots worse than his last visit there) — then the best round anyone has ever played at the Stadium in TEG, 84 gross, a new course record and a personal best by 7, which earned him second in the Jacket and nothing else.
Dropped 22 shots in eight holes on the opening morning and still finished Trophy runner-up, with personal bests at both Camiral courses and a birdie at R4's 17th to stop one last bleed.

venue_notes: TEG's 4th visit to Catalonia and a thoroughly familiar patch of Girona: R1 and R2 were the 5th and 6th TEG rounds on the Tour course, R3 and R4 the 6th and 7th on the Stadium. Lean on the irony that the Tour course — billed as the more forgiving sibling — produced the worst gross round in its TEG history (Alex Baker's 106), while the Stadium, 'Spain's premier golf course', gave up a new course record (Mullin's 84) and then had it matched the next day by Williams. Use the Tour/Stadium switch at the halfway point as the tournament's hinge: everything that mattered in the Jacket and the Spoon was settled two holes into the Stadium.
course_history_notes: Mullin's 84 in R3 is a new PGA Catalunya - Stadium course record across 27 prior TEG visits, his own personal best there by 7, and 8 shots better than his last visit
Williams's 84 in R4 is his personal best at the Stadium by 8 shots — and matches the record Mullin had set the previous day
Patterson set new personal bests at both courses: 94 on the Tour in R2 and 93 on the Stadium in R3
Jon Baker was 8 shots worse than his last visit to the Stadium; Alex Baker 7 worse — the brothers went in opposite directions on the Trophy table anyway
decisive_moments: Trophy: R1 H5 on the Tour course — Alex Baker retakes the outright lead and is never headed over the remaining 67 holes; the 46-point opening round and its 12-point cushion made the last three days an escort job
Green Jacket: R3 H2 at the Stadium — Williams pars to take the lead outright (b09), turns it into 8 clear by nightfall and 14 by the finish
Wooden Spoon: R3 H2 at the Stadium — Jon Baker's triple bogey drops him to the bottom (b31), and 28 and 29 points over the last two rounds ensured he never climbed out

vehicle_fit_response.note: The recovery beats are real but small change; the week's story is a wholesale reversal of standing — TEG 17's Spoon holder in the Jacket, TEG 17's champion holding the Spoon, and a three-time Spooner winning the Trophy — so inversion leads, with the brothers' first-and-last as the dual narrative.
